text:
Kari Oyen reflects on her journey and impact at the University of South Dakota
Kari Oyen, associate professor and program director of the school psychology program at the University of South Dakota, described her professional journey and ongoing commitment to students in a statement released on July 8. Oyen said her connection to USD began early, recalling time spent with her father in the stands of the DakotaDome at age four, which eventually led to a career centered around Coyote pride.
Before joining USD as faculty, Oyen worked as a school psychologist in the Lennox School District. “I loved my time as a practitioner and enjoyed all of the students and families that I got to work with along the way,” Oyen said. “About seven years into my career, I was getting the nudge to learn more and start thinking about the next generation of school psychologists.”
Oyen pursued her Ph.D. at USD after this realization. Upon completing her dissertation, she accepted a tenure-track position within USD’s school psychology program. She has since advanced to associate professor and serves as program director. “It is so fun to walk the same halls that I have walked for many years in a role that allows me to make a difference in the lives of students,” said Oyen. “It has been the honor of my life to be granted tenure at a place that has meant so much to me both personally and professionally.”
Her research focuses on developing successful outcomes for children, impacting local, state, and national initiatives such as supporting rural schools in training new school psychologists and participating on strategic planning efforts for national organizations. “The biggest opportunity that I have as a professor at USD is to have a direct impact on my state and community through my work at the university,” Oyen said.
Oyen is also recognized for her involvement beyond academics; she serves as USD’s faculty athletic representative to the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) while maintaining strong support for student-athletes. Reflecting on student achievements she witnesses across campus roles, Oyen said, “My favorite part of both of my roles is watching students be so successful and achieving their dreams... What a gift it is to be a small part of this journey for students!”
The University offers several unique programs related to social well-being through its Department of Sustainability and Environment—such as degrees in sustainability unavailable elsewhere regionally—and maintains facilities like Akeley-Lawrence Science Center while engaging with broader communities through institutes along local rivers, according to the official website.
